<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as legumes

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers legumes in 6 forms kept separate in every comparison: legumes, as sold (1,013 results), legumes, canned (164 results), legumes, dried (137 results), legumes, frozen (32 results), <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-legumes" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-legumes-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of legumes, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Legumes, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤12.3</td><td>400–520 (bounded)</td><td>835–1150 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤15</td><td>400–520 (bounded)</td><td>835–1150 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>417 reference units; 2 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>415</td><td>50%</td></tr><tr><td>Stančić et al. 2016</td><td>2</td><td>50%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for legumes, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>2 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/stancic2016-varazdin-market-vegetables-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/stancic2016-varazdin-market-vegetables-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Stančić et al. 2016</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:legumes-7105975c1543:fabae01eb355</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. <summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of legumes have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For cadmium, the HMI reference median was lowest for legumes, dried (4.77 µg/kg) and highest for legumes, canned (250 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/yu2023-zhejiang-beans-toxic-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yu S, Pan XD, Han JL · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yu2023-zhejiang-beans-toxic-elements">Toxic Elements in Beans from Zhejiang, Southeast China: Distribution and Probabilistic Health Risk Assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yu2023-zhejiang-beans-toxic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/alsabagh2025-canned-products-baghdad-heavy-metals|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alsabagh AAA · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alsabagh2025-canned-products-baghdad-heavy-metals">Assessment of heavy metal and nitrate contamination in canned products from local markets in Baghdad</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Alnakhla Journal of Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alsabagh2025-canned-products-baghdad-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-legumes" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-legumes" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in legumes?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in legumes?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, legumes, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (1.1 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (90 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in AFRO (1 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (43 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-legumes" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-legumes" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in legumes?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in legumes?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same legumes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Legumes, canned (Legume, Riyadh city markets, May 2009) had lead higher at 19 µg/kg, against 14 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (legumes, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-legumes-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-legumes-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in legumes is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in legumes is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">
